hypotheses.justification: The only use of hf is desiredIncrement_smooth h n hf hp, inside axialPotential_supported. It feeds PressureStream.streamPotential_supported, then RadialPullback.physicalCompact_supported, which uses smoothness only as continuity for TransportPrimitive.canonicalCompact_supported → compactIntegral_supported → pastIntegral_eq_zero_of_le. Every other step (desiredIncrement_supported, temporalInverse_supported, centered_supported, weightedSource_supported, normalizeSource_supported, pullback_supported, divideRadius_supported, streamGamma_supported) needs only the support hypothesis hs. In pastIntegral_eq_zero_of_le, continuity only handles the endpoint u = 0 when z.1 = a. For u < 0, (shift M v z u).1 = z.1 + u < a, so the integrand vanishes by the support hypothesis alone. The single point {0} has Lebesgue measure zero, so ∫ u in Iic 0, ... = 0 for any g: use MeasureTheory.integral_Iic_eq_integral_Iio and then setIntegral_eq_zero_of_forall_eq_zero, or setIntegral_eq_zero_of_ae_eq_zero. The right edge (pastIntegral_eq_total_of_ge) already needs no continuity. So the conclusion follows from hs, ha, hab and hd for arbitrary f. Deleting hf alone works; hf and hp can also be deleted together.

hp is used only in desiredIncrement_smooth h n hf hp, to get smoothness of desiredIncrement. As argued for hf, that smoothness is needed only as continuity in pastIntegral_eq_zero_of_le, where an almost-everywhere argument replaces it: the integrand vanishes for u < 0 by the support hypothesis, and {0} is Lebesgue-null (MeasureTheory.integral_Iic_eq_integral_Iio, then setIntegral_eq_zero_of_forall_eq_zero). The rest of the support chain (desiredIncrement_supported, temporalInverse_supported, centered_supported, weightedSource_supported, normalizeSource_supported, pullback_supported, divideRadius_supported, streamGamma_supported) uses only hs. So the radial support of axialUpdate holds without hp. hp can be deleted on its own, or together with hf.
